Actor.description: Ignored since 1.1: the audit actor and `provenance.agent` are the authenticated principal.
Actor.name: x-memhouse-actor

Csrf.description: The session's CSRF token (`csrf_token` of `GET /v1/session`). Every request made with the session cookie that is not a `GET` must carry it; a request made with a key or token does not.
Csrf.name: x-memhouse-csrf

IdempotencyKey.description: 1 to 255 characters. A repeat with the same key and request returns the first response; the same key with another request is a 409. Same as the body's `request_key`.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

User.description: The user the call acts for. Accepted only from admins and from agents trusted to act for users (`act_as`); a user's key always acts for that user, a token for its own user.
User.name: x-memhouse-user

Admission.description: How proposals from agents without a commit grant are admitted (GOV-08).

oneOf.description: The engine commits a proposal as soon as it passes the write gate.

Proposals stay `candidate` until a principal with `memory:review` commits or rejects them.
Conversation rounds (`ingest`) are always admitted by the engine.

AdvisorMeasure.description: How one measured value stands against the limit of the profile (PROF-11).

detail.description: What the value counts, and for `largest_subject_records` which subject.

limit.description: The limit the profile is measured at or configured with; absent: reported, not judged.

status.description: `ok`, `near_limit` (at or above `[advisor] warn_at` of the limit) or `over_limit`.

command.description: The command that moves the installation to the recommended profile.

recommendation.description: What to do, when a measure is near or over its limit.

status.description: The worst status among the measures: `ok`, `near_limit` or `over_limit`.

warn_at.description: The share of a limit from which a measure is `near_limit`.

Approver.description: Who commits a candidate of a type.

oneOf.description: Any principal with `memory:review`.
An admin principal with `memory:review`.

CodeRef.description: A file a memory is about (TR-TPL-02): stale when the file's content hash changes.

blob_hash.description:
The content hash of the file when the memory was written or last revalidated: the git
blob hash by convention (`git hash-object`).

path.description: The file's path in the repository, with `/` separators, relative to its root.

seen_hash.description:
The content hash the file was last seen with while stale; absent when it was deleted.
Set by the server, ignored on a write.

stale_since.description:
Set by the server when the file was seen with other content, or deleted (TPL-04): the
memory is then left out of default recall until it is revalidated or revised. Ignored
on a write.

CompiledPolicy.description: A compiled policy and the version records and traces are stamped with.

version.description:
`gov-<hash>` for the default policy, `policy-v<n>-<hash>` for an approved spec,
`draft-<hash>` for one only validated. The hash is of the body, so equal policies get
equal versions on every node.

CompiledPolicyBody.description: Everything a policy decides, with nothing left unset: the body stored in `mh_policy`.

decisions.description: Access-decision values (D-01…D-07), from the decision register in G28.

languages.description: The languages the tenant's text is detected among; absent means every enabled one.

spec.description: The spec it was compiled from; absent for the default policy (the configuration).

types.description: Each type's gate, retention, retrieval method and access rules (MEM-01).

EffectivePreference.description:
A preference as it applies to a reader (`GET /v1/subjects/{subject}/preferences`, MEM-04):
for each key, the one set at the narrowest scope the reader is in.

key.description:
The preference's key (`structured.attrs.key` of a `preference` record); absent for a
preference written as text only, which overrides nothing.

level.description: The scope level it is set at.

overrides.description: The same preference at broader levels, which this one overrides.

oldest_pending_secs.description: Age of the oldest pending job, in seconds (queue lag).

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error response.

error.description: What went wrong, for people. The wording may change between releases.

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error codes. Clients branch on these, never on the message text.

oneOf.description: The request is malformed or fails validation (400).
Missing or wrong API key (401).
The caller is known but may not do this (403).
The record (or route) doesn't exist (404).

The request conflicts with the stored state: an idempotency key reused for another
request, or a revision of a record that is no longer the current version (409).
A failure inside MemHouse or its database or models (500).

A dependency is down for now (the intake queue, the database): retry later (503, with
`Retry-After`). Nothing was written (PERF-07).

EvalMetrics.description:
The quality metrics of a replay, each 0 to 1; `None` when the suite has nothing to measure it
on (no question, no correction, no plan).

contamination_rate.description: Of the plans and guesses, the part committed as facts.

retrieval_precision.description: Of the questions, the part whose first hit is the current fact.

retrieval_recall.description: Of the questions, the part with the current fact in the top k.

stale_rate.description: Of the questions about a corrected fact, the part answered with a stale version in the top k.

stale_withheld.description:
Of the questions about a memory whose file changed since, the part where it was
withheld (suites with code).

storage_precision.description: Of the scored records committed and valid at a checkpoint, the part that are current facts.

storage_recall.description: Of the current facts at a checkpoint, the part that is stored.

touched_recall.description:
Of the file-touched questions about a memory that is not stale, the part answered with
it among the linked memories (suites with code).

EvalRunInfo.description: One stored replay without its per-conversation detail (`GET /v1/eval/runs`).

gate_passed.description: For a replay made by the regression gate: whether the gate passed.

policy_version.description: The policy version the replay ran under.

EvalSuiteInfo.description: A stored evaluation suite without its conversations (`GET /v1/eval/suites`).

oneOf.description: Asked for (`memhouse eval run`).
A policy version waiting for approval, and the active policy it is compared with.
The engine or a model changed (`memhouse eval gate`).

ExactQuery.description: An exact structured-record query inside a recall (HYB-02, HYB-03).

attrs.description: A JSON object the record's attributes must contain (`{"order_id": "A-1001"}`).

record_type.description: Only records of this type (`order`, `address`, ...); any type when absent.

ExcludedRecord.description: A record left out of a recall, and why.

detail.description: Identifiers and values only, never content (e.g. `label hr`, `valid_to 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`).

ExclusionReason.description: Why a record that matched a recall's query is not among its results (GOV-04).

oneOf.description: Not recallable in its state: quarantined, candidate, rejected, expired, or superseded.
Scoped to another user, agent, team or org than the caller.
Carries a label denied to the caller.

Not valid at the recall's time: before `valid_from`, after `valid_to` or `expires_at`, or
happened after `as_of`.
A file the memory is about changed since it was written or last revalidated (TPL-04).
Outside the request's own filters: kinds, tags or time window.
A procedure that does not match the task the recall is for (MEM-02).
A preference overridden by the same preference at a narrower scope (MEM-04).
A near-duplicate of a better-ranked memory in the same recall (ECON-03).
Cut by the token budget.
Ranked below the `k` returned.

FileState.description:
What a file of a repository was seen as (TPL-04): its current content hash, or deleted, or
renamed from another path.

blob_hash.description:
The file's current content hash (the git blob hash by convention). A file named
without one, and not `deleted`, is only looked up: nothing is recorded about it.

path.description: The file's path in the repository, with `/` separators, relative to its root.

renamed_from.description:
The path the file had before it was renamed to `path`: references to the old path move
to the new one, and are stale only if the content changed too.

FileTouchedRequest.description:
An agent opened or edited files of a repository (`POST /v1/code/touched`, TPL-05): the
staleness of the memories linked to them is updated from the hashes, and the linked
memories are returned.

files.description:
The files, each with its current content hash. A file given as `deleted` or with
`renamed_from` is handled as in `POST /v1/code/changed`; one given by its path alone
is looked up without recording anything about it.

query.description:
What the agent is doing, in natural language. With it, procedures that match the task
and are not linked to the files are returned too (`related`, task-matched retrieval).

render.description: Also return the memories as a text block ready for a prompt.

subject.description: The repository (`repo:<name>` in the coding template).

FileTouchedResult.description: The memories linked to the touched files.

changes.description:
What this request changed: references flagged stale, cleared or moved by a rename, of
memories the caller may recall.

memories.description:
Linked memories whose files have the content they were written about: every one the
caller may recall, however many there are.

needs_revalidation.description:
Linked memories whose file changed since: left out of default recall until each is
revalidated (`POST /v1/code/revalidate`), revised or forgotten.

related.description: Procedures that match `query` and are not linked to the files (only with `query`).

rendered.description: `memories` and `related` as one text block, with `render`.

FilesChangedRequest.description:
Files changed outside the agent's view (`POST /v1/code/changed`, TPL-04): a commit, a
checkout, a merge. Staleness is marked for every file named, opened or not.

files.description: Changed files with their new content hash, deleted files, renamed files.

reason.description: What produced the change, for the audit log: a commit id, `checkout`, ...

subject.description: The repository (`repo:<name>` in the coding template).

FilesChangedResult.description: What a batch of file changes did.

changes.description: References flagged stale, cleared or moved, of memories the caller may recall.

cleared.description:
Memories that were stale and are no longer (every file they are about was seen with
its stored content again), among those the caller may recall.

flagged.description:
Memories that became stale with this request (they were not stale before it), among
those the caller may recall.

ForgetRequest.description:
Delete memories (`forget`, CORE-05). Name exactly one of `id`, `subject`, `user`, `agent`,
`source`, `untrusted` or `all`. Deletion is permanent and includes every derived representation.

agent.description: Records written by the agent or scoped to it, in any subject.

all.description: The whole tenant. Needs `confirm` set to the tenant's name.

confirm.description: The tenant's name, when `all` is set.

dry_run.description: Count what would be deleted, delete nothing.

id.description: One record (and the facts derived from it).

request_key.description: Idempotency key: a repeat returns the first result instead of `not_found`.

source.description: Records with this source label, in any subject.

subject.description: Everything held about a subject (right to erasure).

untrusted.description:
Candidates held because their source is not trusted (GOV-10): those of this source
label, or of every untrusted source with `*`.

user.description: Records the user wrote through an agent or that are scoped to the user, in any subject.

deleted.description:
Records deleted (or, with `dry_run`, that would be: a match a legal hold keeps is counted
under `held`, not here). Facts derived from them are deleted too and are not counted
unless they match themselves.

deletion_id.description:
The deletion request (absent for a dry run): `memhouse deletion certificate <id>` prints
its completion certificate.

held.description:
Records the request matches that a legal hold keeps (GOV-09). The request stays open
while any hold that applies to them is active, and they are deleted when the last one
is released.

value.description: The id, subject, user, agent, source or tenant named.

Grant.description:
One agent's agent-scoped memory made readable to another agent (INT-06). Without a grant an
agent never reads records scoped to another agent.

grantee.description: The agent that may read it.

grantor.description: The agent whose memory is shared.

kinds.description: Kinds the grant covers; empty is all.

subjects.description: Subjects the grant covers: an exact name, a prefix ending in `*`, or `*` for all.

exact.description: Found by an exact structured-record match (HYB-02), not by similarity.

score.description: Fused score; compare it only within one response.

similarity.description: Cosine similarity of the best vector.

working.description:
From the working memory of the recall's session (MEM-01): listed first, newest first, not
ranked against the query.

IngestRequest.description: Store a conversation as episodic memory, one record per user/assistant round.

per_message.description:
Store every message as its own record instead of grouping user/assistant rounds
(use for multi-party conversations without a "user" role).

session_id.description: Groups the rounds; also the unit of background enrichment. Defaults to a new id.

session_time.description: Session start time; used for messages without their own timestamp.

wait.description: Wait until the rounds are stored, as for `remember`.

ids.description: Ids of the rounds stored (or queued).

queued.description:
True while the rounds are still in the intake queue (the request did not set `wait`):
their ids resolve to `candidate` until the pipeline has stored them.

refused.description:
Rounds left out because the policy refuses them (a category set to `reject`): not
stored, not queued. The other rounds are. Text over the limit is shortened and stored.

stored.description: Rounds stored; while `queued`, the rounds accepted into the intake queue.

KeyCreated.description: A new key. `key` is the only time its secret is shown: nothing stores it.

key.description: The full key, `mh_<id>_<secret>`: send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

replaces.description: For a rotation: the key it replaces and until when that one works.

KeyInfo.description: An API key as the API shows it: never its secret or the hash of it.

id.description: The public id of the key (the middle part of `mh_<id>_<secret>`).

state.description: `active`, `expired` or `revoked`, at the time of the answer.

KeyRequest.description: Create a key for a principal (`POST /v1/keys`).

expires_in_secs.description: Lifetime in seconds. Default: no expiry.

scopes.description:
The permissions the key carries. Default: every permission the principal's kind allows
that the calling credential carries itself. A key never carries more than its maker.

KeyRevoked.description: The answer to revoking a key.

grace_secs.description: How long the old key keeps working, in seconds. Default: 86400 (a day); 0 ends it now.

LinkedMemory.description: A memory linked to a file, with the state of that link (TPL-05).

code_refs.description: The memory's references to the paths the request named.

expires_at.description: After this the record is no longer recalled (working memory, MEM-01).

language.description:
The language the text was detected as, among the enabled ones (a language-pack code
such as `en` or `de`); absent on records written before languages were recorded.

occurred_at.description: When the remembered thing happened (event time), if known.

source.description: Source label: the writer by default, `enrich:<model>` for extracted facts.

stale_since.description:
Set while a file the memory is about has other content than when the memory was written
or last revalidated (TPL-04): the memory is left out of default recall.

status.description:
Lifecycle state. A recall returns `committed` records, and `candidate` ones only when it
asks with `include_candidates`: check this field before treating such a hit as admitted.

supersedes.description: The previous version, which this record replaced.

valid_to.description: When it stopped being true; set when it is superseded.

oneOf.description: Short-lived task context for one session; expires (MEM-01).
Raw conversation history: a user/assistant round.
Durable facts about the subject.
Likes, dislikes, ways of working.
How-to knowledge, conventions, procedures.
Promises, follow-ups, open items with a due date.
Reference documents or snippets.

The organisation's own terms and classifications: agents propose, an administrator
approves (MEM-03).

MemoryPage.description:
One page of a list. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is absent on the
last page. Cursors are opaque.

MemoryStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a record (CORE-02). By default only `committed` records are recalled; a recall
that asks with `include_candidates` also returns `candidate` ones, each labelled by its status.

```text
candidate ──► committed ──► superseded
    │  │          │  └────► expired
    │  └► rejected │
    └──► quarantined ◄┘ ──► rejected   (quarantined ──► committed on release)
```

oneOf.description: Proposed, waiting for its gate (asynchronous admission, G10).
Replaced by a newer version (`superseded_by`).
Held back by the gate (for example an injected instruction).
Refused by the gate or a reviewer.
Past `expires_at` (working memory, commitments).

Message.description: One message of a conversation handed to `ingest`.

id.description: Caller's own reference for the message (for provenance and evaluation).

role.description: `user`, `assistant`, or a participant's name in a multi-party conversation.

timestamp.description: When the message was sent; defaults to the request's `session_time`.

Partition.description: Whose partition a write of a type lands in (ACC-10).

oneOf.description: The subject the write names: a note about a patient is stored with the patient.

The verified user the write is made for: their own preferences and procedures are stored
with them, whatever subject the conversation was about.

PolicyActivation.description: One activation: what ran from then on.

compiled.description: The compiled policy version records were stamped with from then on.

version.description: The spec version activated; absent for the default policy.

PolicyChange.description: One changed setting between two compiled policies.

PolicyDiff.description: The settings that differ between two compiled policies.

from.description: `default` or a version (`3`, `v3`); absent: the policy running now.

spec.description: A spec to compare, compiled but not stored.

to.description: `default` or a version; give this or `spec`.

dedup.description: Near-duplicate removal in packing (ECON-03) and its two thresholds.

relevance_weight.description:
Weights of the final score's features (HYB-05): relevance, confidence and validity next
to `recency_weight`. Bodies compiled before they existed rank by relevance and recency.

actions.description: The action of each category that is not simply redacted (GOV-05).

scopes.description: Rules for one type within one scope (GOV-06), which win over the type's own.

PolicyRetentionScope.description: Retention of one memory type within one scope (GOV-06).

days.description:
Days after which the scope's records of the type are purged; 0 keeps them whatever the
type's own rule says. For `episodic`, within governance's limit.

kind.description: The memory type; not `working`, which expires by its TTL.

value.description: The subject, org, team, agent, user or session the rule is for.

PolicySpec.description:
A behaviour policy as authored (TOML or JSON). Every section and field is optional: what a spec
leaves out keeps the governance or configured value.

language.description: The languages the tenant's text is read in (G36).

name.description: A short name: letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

types.description: Per-type rules (MEM-01): one optional section per memory type.

enabled.description:
Some of the server's enabled languages (`[language] enabled`): the tenant's writes and
questions are detected among these only. It narrows what statements are read as, never
the injection screen, which always applies every enabled language's phrases.

allowed.description: Kinds that may be written; writes of other kinds are refused. Default: all.

PolicySpecRanking.description: Ranking weights (the meaning of each is in `[memory]` of the configuration reference).

dedup.description: Leave near-duplicates out of a recall (ECON-03).

audit_reads.description: Audit every recall; can't be turned off where governance turns it on.

denied_labels.description: Labels never read; must include every label governance denies.

actions.description:
What happens to a match, by category (GOV-05): `mask`, `redact` or `reject`. A policy
may make a category's action stricter than governance's (mask < redact < reject), never
looser.

categories.description: Categories redacted before anything is stored; must include every governance category.

PolicySpecRef.description: The approved spec a compiled policy came from.

version.description: The spec's version number; absent for a draft that was only validated.

note.description: Why the change is proposed (kept with the version).

episodic_days.description:
Days after which episodic memory is purged; 0 keeps it. Where governance purges, at most
its days and never 0.

scopes.description:
Retention of one memory type within one scope (GOV-06): `[[retention.scopes]]` with
`level`, `value`, `kind` and `days`. Where two rules match a record, the more specific
level wins (session, user, agent, team, org, subject), and any of them wins over the
type's own `retention_days`.

working_ttl_secs.description: Lifetime of working memory written without `expires_at` (1 second to 30 days).

PolicySpecScope.description: What the policy governs. v1: one tenant (layers by org, team and agent come in G24).

oneOf.description: Stored, not yet approved: it never executes.
Approved by a named approver; may be activated (and rolled back to).

PolicySpecType.description: One type's section of a spec (`[types.semantic]`): what it leaves out keeps the type's default.

gate.description:
A gate at least as strict as the type's own (`none` < `source` < `full` = `explicit` <
`confirmation` < `approval`).

retention_days.description:
Days after which records of the type are purged; 0 keeps them. For `episodic`, within
governance's limit. Not for `working`, which expires by `ttl_secs`.

ttl_secs.description: `working` only: seconds a record lives after its session's last write (1 second to 30 days).

agent_private.description:
Scope agents' writes of this type to the writing agent. May be turned on, not off where it
is the type's default.

approver.description: `admin` anywhere; `reviewer` only where it is the type's default.

admission.description: `auto` or `review`; `auto` only where governance doesn't require review.

corrections.description:
Whether a correction, or the same statement with a changed value, supersedes what it
updates (QUAL-01; the default). With `false` both versions stay current: for tenants that
keep every statement as it was made. The regression gate measures what that costs.

dedup_threshold.description: Cosine similarity at which a new memory counts as a duplicate (0.5 to 1).

quarantine_injection.description: Always on (security baseline); may be stated, never turned off.

untrusted_sources.description:
Source patterns added to those governance does not trust (GOV-10): a write from a
matching source waits for a reviewer. A policy may add patterns, never remove them.

PolicyStatus.description: The active policy of a tenant, its spec versions and its activations.

active.description: The spec version activated last; absent while the default policy runs.

running.description: The compiled policy that runs now.

warning.description:
Set when the active spec no longer compiles under the current governance, so the default
policy runs instead.

PolicyType.description: The rules of one memory type (MEM-01).

retention_days.description: Days after which records of the type are purged; 0 keeps them until superseded or deleted.

ttl_secs.description: Working memory: seconds a record lives after its session's last write.

agent_private.description:
An agent's writes of this type are scoped to that agent: other agents read them only with
a grant (INT-06).

PolicyTypes.description: The rules of every memory type.

PolicyValidation.description: Whether a spec compiles for the caller's tenant, and to what.

PolicyViolation.description: A setting that doesn't compile, and why.

corrections.description: Corrections and changed values supersede what they update (QUAL-01).

untrusted_sources.description: Source patterns whose writes wait for a reviewer (GOV-10).

PrincipalInfo.description: A principal as the API shows it (`GET /v1/principals`).

act_as.description: May state which user it acts for.

can_commit.description: Agents only: writes commit directly instead of being proposed (GOV-08).

denied_labels.description: Labels it may never read or write.

disabled_at.description: Set while the principal is disabled: its keys, tokens and sessions are refused.

kinds.description: Memory kinds it may use; empty is all.

subjects.description: Subjects it may use: exact names or prefixes ending in `*`; `*` is all.

oneOf.description: Software acting for users: proposes memories, recalls them.
A person, calling directly or through an agent it delegates to.
Operates the deployment: erasure, review, audit.

PrincipalRequest.description:
Create a principal or replace its attributes (`PUT /v1/principals/{id}`). The kind is the
prefix of the id. Every field is the whole new value: one left out takes its default,
except `name`, which is then kept.

act_as.description: May state which user it acts for (a backend that authenticates its users).

can_commit.description: Agents only: commit writes directly instead of proposing them (GOV-08).

denied_labels.description: Labels it may never read or write.

kinds.description: Memory kinds it may use. Default: all.

name.description:
A display name. The one field that is kept when left out: absent, `null` or empty
leaves the principal's current name as it is (a name is replaced, never cleared).

subjects.description: Subjects it may use: exact names or prefixes ending in `*`. Default: `["*"]`, all.

PromoteRequest.description:
Promote memories to another type (`POST /v1/promote`, MEM-05): a new record of `kind` in the
same subject, through that type's own gate, linked to its sources (`metadata.promoted_from`)
and audited (`memory.promote`). The sources stay as they are.

content.description:
The promoted memory's text. Required for several sources; for one it defaults to the
source's text.

kind.description:
The type of the new record: `semantic`, `preference`, `procedural` or `taxonomic`, or
`episodic` for working memory.

labels.description: Labels added to the sources' own, which the new record always keeps.

scope.description:
The new record's scope. Defaults to the sources' common scope without its session, so
promoting out of a session's working memory makes the memory visible to the session's user.

sources.description: The records promoted: 1 to 50 committed records of one subject.

wait.description: Wait for the write gate, as for `remember`.

Provenance.description:
Who and what admitted a record (GOV-03), and which model derived it (TR-MS-02). The source
turn is the record's `session_id` and `turn_ref`; its confidence is `confidence`.

extractor.description: For derived records: the model that extracted it, and its prompt and configuration.

policy_version.description: The compiled policy that admitted the record (`mh_policy`; `legacy-v1` before schema v2).

request_key.description: The client's idempotency key for the request that wrote it (CORE-06).

user.description: The user the agent acted for, when known.

exact.description:
Identifiers in the question ("A-1001", "#4521") looked up exactly in structured records
(HYB-03): the plan then mixes keyword, vector and exact retrieval.

RankFeatures.description: What a hit's final score was combined from (HYB-05), each before its policy weight.

recency.description: 1 for a memory of now, halving towards 0 with age (`1 / (1 + age / half_life)`).

relevance.description: Keyword and vector ranks fused, or the reranker's score.

validity.description: 1 for a confirmed record valid now, 0.5 for a candidate, 0 for one no longer valid.

RecallExplanation.description:
A recall's explanation (`GET /v1/recalls/{id}/explanation`, GOV-04): what it returned and why,
and the records that matched the query but were left out, each with its reason. Exclusions for
access, labels and state are recomputed from the store when the explanation is read
(`replayed_at`); budget and rank cuts are as recorded.

excluded.description: Most relevant first, by reason order (status, access, label, validity, filter, budget, rank).

hidden.description:
Excluded records this viewer may not know about, counted by reason (ids are shown only to
principals with `audit:read`).

RecallRecord.description: What a recall was asked, how it was authorized and what it returned, kept for its explanation.

authorizer.description: The authorizer that decided (`scope`; `rebac` from G27).

cut.description: Records the recall itself cut (budget, rank); the explanation adds the rest.

include_stale.description:
The recall did not leave out memories whose file had changed: it asked with
`include_stale`, or with `as_of`. It says what was asked, not that such a memory was
among the results.

scope.description: The scope filter applied (the caller's own, merged with the request's).

shared_agents.description: Agents whose memory the caller was granted when it recalled (INT-06).

valid_at.description: The time validity was checked at.

RecallRequest.description: Retrieve memories for a context (`recall`, CORE-03).

analyze.description: Override query analysis (time windows and sub-queries) on/off.

as_of.description: Recall what was true at this time (validity and event-time filter).

exact.description:
An exact query over structured records (HYB-02): records of this type whose attributes
contain these values are returned first, matched exactly, never by similarity.

include_candidates.description:
Also return candidates (plans and speculation the gate holds, proposals waiting for
review), each labelled by its `status` (PR-7). Default recall never returns them.

include_stale.description:
Also return memories whose file changed since they were written (TPL-04), each marked
by its `stale_since`. Default recall leaves them out until they are revalidated.

k.description: Number of memories to return (default `memory.default_k`, at most 200).

paths.description:
Files the task at hand touches (repository paths). A procedure linked to one of them
matches the task whatever the query says (task-matched retrieval, MEM-02).

query.description: What you need to know, in natural language.

reference_time.description:
"Now" for reading relative time in the query ("two weeks ago"). Defaults to `as_of`, then
the current time. Unlike `as_of` it filters nothing.

render.description: Also return the memories as a text block ready for a prompt (`rendered`, INT-04).

render_format.description:
The form of the text block: `plain` (the default), `markdown` or `xml`. Naming one also
asks for the block, like `render`.

scope.description:
Only memories visible in this scope: each scope field the request sets matches records
with the same value or none (scope inheritance, MEM-04). `scope.session` names the session
the recall runs in: its working memory comes first, and records of other sessions are never
returned.

subject.description: Whose memory to search. Recall never crosses subjects.

tags.description: Only memories with at least one of these tags.

token_budget.description:
A hard cap, in approximate tokens (4 bytes each), on the content of the returned
memories and on the rendered block (PERF-06). A memory that does not fit is left out.

degraded.description:
Set when retrieval failed or ran out of time: `hits` is then empty, not a real answer
(PERF-07). The value says why; callers should go on without memory, not retry in a loop.

embed_ms.description: Time spent embedding the query, in the SQL statement, and reranking.

hits.description: Ranked memories, most relevant first, each with its id and provenance.

plan.description: How the query was read: time windows and sub-queries that got their own retrieval probe.

recall_id.description: Id of this recall's explanation (`GET /v1/recalls/{id}/explanation`, GOV-04).

rendered.description: The hits as a model-neutral text block, when the request set `render`.

RecallStages.description: Time spent per stage of a recall.

instrument_ms.description:
Time the recall spent on its own instrumentation: metrics and this record (the row itself is
written off the request path).

probes.description: Probes run in that statement: the query, plus a time window or sub-queries it mentions.

statements.description: Database round trips on the synchronous path (PERF-02).

RedactAction.description:
What the write gate does with a match of a redaction category (GOV-05). In order of
strictness: a policy may raise a category's action, never lower it.

RefChange.description: What an observation did to one code reference (see `Store::code_refs_observe`).

cleared.description: The reference was stale and the file was seen again with the stored content.

flagged.description: The reference became stale with this observation.

id.description: The memory the reference belongs to.

moved_from.description: The path it had before a rename moved it.

path.description: The reference's path, after a rename.

stale.description: Whether the memory has any stale reference after the observation.

was_stale.description:
Whether the memory had a stale reference before the observation: it became stale with
this request when `stale` is true and this is false.

RelabelRequest.description:
Replace a record's sensitivity labels (`POST /v1/labels`, ACC-04). No new version and no
re-embedding.

labels.description: The complete new set of labels.

actor.description:
Who makes the change, for the audit log; defaults to the `x-memhouse-actor` header. From
API keys per principal (G06) the authenticated principal is used instead.

code_refs.description: Files the memory is about, for staleness checks.

content.description: The memory, written so it stands alone (who, what, when), ideally one fact.

expires_at.description: When it stops being recalled; `working` memory defaults to now + `memory.working_ttl_secs`.

labels.description: Sensitivity labels (ACC-04); `governance.denied_labels` keeps them out of recall.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON object, stored as given.

occurred_at.description: When the remembered thing happened; defaults to now.

request_key.description:
Idempotency key (or the `Idempotency-Key` header): a repeat with the same key and request
returns the first result; the same key with another request is a conflict (CORE-06).

source.description: Source label; defaults to the actor.

structured.description: The queryable form of the record (an order, a ticket), under the same id.

subject.description: Whose memory it is, e.g. `user:alice`, `customer:42`, `repo:api`. Defaults to the configured subject.

supersedes.description: Replace an existing memory with this one; prefer `revise`.

tags.description: Free tags, usable as recall filters.

tenant.description: The tenant; defaults to the configured one.

user.description: The user the calling agent acts for (provenance).

valid_to.description: When it stops being true (a due date, an expiry).

wait.description:
Wait for the write gate before answering (at most `intake.wait_timeout_ms`): the result
then carries the record's final state. By default `remember` answers as soon as the
redacted write is durably queued, with `status: candidate` (CORE-02).

RememberResult.description:
What a write did. The id is returned at once; `status` says the record's state, which can
also be read later with `GET /v1/memories/{id}` (CORE-02).

deduplicated.description: True when an equivalent memory already existed and nothing new was written.

id.description: The record's id. For a deduplicated write, the id of the memory already stored.

note.description: Why the write was deduplicated, held, quarantined or rejected.

redactions.description: Kinds of sensitive data redacted from the text (`card`, `secret`, ...).

route.description: The representation the record was routed to (HYB-01), once the gate has run.

statement.description: What the gate read the statement as (QUAL-02), once it has run.

status.description:
`candidate` while the write waits for the gate (the default answer); with `wait`, the
gate's decision: `committed`, `candidate` (a plan or speculation held until confirmed, or a
proposal waiting for review), `quarantined` or `rejected`. Clients must not assume a write
is committed: read `GET /v1/memories/{id}` for its state.

RenderFormat.description: The form of a recall's rendered text block (INT-04).

oneOf.description: One line per memory: `- [id] (kind, date #tags) text`.
A Markdown list under a heading.
One `<memory>` element per memory inside `<memories>`, with the text escaped.

Retrieval.description: How a type is retrieved (MEM-01). Set by the engine per type; shown in the compiled policy.

oneOf.description:
A session's records come first in its recalls, newest first, from the session cache
(PERF-05); outside a session they are found by hybrid search until they expire.
Hybrid search with a probe for the time the question names.
Hybrid search plus exact lookup of structured records.

Hybrid search, then the same preference at a narrower scope replaces the broader one;
`GET /v1/subjects/{subject}/preferences` lists them in scope order.
Matched to the task at hand (from G19); hybrid search until then.
Exact lookup of the term's structured form; also found by hybrid search.

ReturnedRecord.description: A record a recall returned, with its ranking signals.

features.description: What the score was combined from, each before its policy weight (HYB-05).

RevalidateRequest.description:
Confirm that a memory still holds for the files as they are now (`POST /v1/code/revalidate`,
TPL-04): its references take the new hashes and it returns to default recall.

code_refs.description:
The references to revalidate, each with the file's current content hash. Without it,
every stale reference takes the hash its file was last seen with; a reference to a
deleted file has none, so the memory must be revised (or forgotten) instead.
The memory's code references after the revalidation.

stale.description: Whether any reference is still stale (only some were revalidated).

ReviewRequest.description: Commit or reject a candidate (`POST /v1/review`, GOV-08, GOV-11).

content.description:
With `commit`: approve this wording instead of the record's own (GOV-11). The text is
written as the reviewer's and passes the write gate like any write; the reviewed
record is then rejected and names its replacement. The way to approve a quarantined
record, which is never committed as it stands.

reason.description: Why, for the audit log (a rejection's reason).

rephrased_from.description:
For a rephrased approval: the reviewed record, now `rejected`; `id` is then the record
that holds the new wording.

status.description: `committed`, or `rejected` (also when a revision's predecessor is no longer current).

ReviseRequest.description:
Correct a memory (`revise`, CORE-04): a new version that supersedes the current one. Fields
left out are taken from the current version (kind, tags, labels, scope, metadata, validity,
structured form, code references).

id.description: The memory to revise; it must be the current (`committed`) version.

wait.description: Wait for the write gate, as for `remember`.

to.description: `default` or an approved version; absent: the policy active before the current one.

Route.description: The representation intake routes a record to (HYB-01).

oneOf.description: Conversation or longer prose: text with keyword and vector search.
One self-contained statement: text search plus correction and duplicate checks.

A record with attributes (an order, an address): also a row in the structured table,
answered by exact query (HYB-02).
A statement relating people or organisations; stored as a fact until the graph (G35).

Source code or a change to it; stored as text with the `code` tag until code-aware
memory (G19).

Scope.description:
Narrower visibility inside a subject (MEM-04). All empty means the whole subject (the tenant
level). Levels inherit broadest to narrowest: tenant, org, team, agent, user, session; a
preference set at a narrower level overrides the same preference at a broader one.

ScopeLevel.description: The levels of a scope, broadest first (MEM-04). Each level inherits from those before it.

ScopeLevel2.description: A scope level a retention rule can name (GOV-06): the subject, or a level of the record's scope.

closed.description: False when the session had ended already.

SessionInfo.description:
A console session (`POST` and `GET /v1/session`). The session itself is the cookie the
answer sets; nothing here is a credential except `csrf_token`, which only works with it.

csrf_token.description: Send as `x-memhouse-csrf` with every request that changes something.

expires_at.description: When the session ends whatever its use.

idle_secs.description: The session also ends when unused for this long; 0: no idle limit.

scopes.description: The permissions of the key that opened the session.

Statement.description:
What a statement asserts, as the write gate reads it (QUAL-02). Plans and speculation stay
candidates until confirmed or expired (PR-7); a correction supersedes what it corrects.

oneOf.description: Something true now ("Acme's renewal date is 1 March").
Something that happened ("The user adopted a cat in March").
A change to, or fix of, something stored before ("Actually, she moved to Porto").
An intention not yet carried out ("The user plans to visit Japan in May").
A guess, rumour or hypothetical ("He might switch vendors").
A like, dislike or way of working.
How something should be done ("Run the tests before every commit").

Structured.description: The queryable form of a structured record (HYB-02), under the same id as its text.

attrs.description: A JSON object of attributes, queried exactly, never by similarity.

SubjectCount.description: A subject and its number of committed memories.

SuiteTrend.description: The quality metrics of one suite by policy version, oldest version first (QUAL-11).

meaning.description: What the phrase resolves to, for people and answer models ("2023-04-15 (Sat)").

phrase.description: The phrase the window was read from.

TokenRequest.description: Ask for a short-lived agent token (`POST /v1/tokens`, GOV-13).

agent.description:
The agent principal the token acts as. Required when a user or an admin asks; an agent
gets a token for itself.

scopes.description: Narrower permissions than the caller's; defaults to all the caller may pass on.

ttl_secs.description: At most `access.token_ttl_secs` (default and maximum 900 unless configured, never above 3600).

user.description:
The user the token acts for. A user's token always acts for that user; an admin or an
agent trusted to act for users (`act_as`) may name one.

agent.description: The agent principal the token acts as.

user.description: The user it acts for, if any.

TrendPoint.description: A suite's quality under one policy version: the latest replay that ran under it.

metrics.description: The metrics of the latest replay under this version.

runs.description: Replays stored under this version (within the runs read).

TypeGate.description:
What a write of a type must pass before it is committed (MEM-01), loosest first. The
injection screen and redaction are not part of it: they apply to every type (security
baseline).

oneOf.description: Committed as written: no statement gate, no duplicate check, no review (working memory).

Committed when its source is verified: the writer is an authenticated principal and the
record says where it came from (episodic memory). What was said is not judged.

The statement gate (QUAL-02): plans and speculation are held, duplicates rejected,
corrections supersede (semantic memory).

The statement gate, and only explicit statements commit: a write marked as an inferred
signal (`metadata.signal`) is held until the same signal has been seen
`intake.preference_signals` times (preferences).

The statement gate, and a proposal waits for explicit confirmation by a reviewer even
where proposals are otherwise admitted automatically (procedural memory, MEM-02).

The statement gate, and only the type's approver commits: everyone else proposes
(taxonomic memory, MEM-03).

scope.description:
The caller's own scope (MEM-04): its org, team, agent and user. Reads return records of
these and of broader levels. Empty for an admin, who reads every scope.

user.description: The verified user the calls act for.

post.description: Marks staleness in batch (TPL-04), what a post-commit hook calls: for files the agent never opened too. A changed file carries its new content hash, a deleted one `deleted`, a renamed one `renamed_from` and its hash. A memory with a stale reference is left out of default recall until it is revalidated, revised or forgotten. The answer lists the changes to memories a recall could give the caller now (committed, valid, unexpired); `flagged` and `cleared` count the memories whose staleness this request changed (`was_stale` against `stale`), not the references. References and their audit events are written in one transaction. Needs `memory:write`. Audited as `memory.stale`, `memory.fresh` and `memory.code_moved`.

post.description: Revalidation (TPL-04): code references of the memory take a hash the caller vouches for and are no longer stale. With `code_refs`, only the references named take the given hashes (a partial revalidation: `stale` in the answer stays true while another reference is stale, and the memory returns to default recall only when none is); without, every stale reference takes the hash its file was last seen with, which is the checked content only if nothing changed the file since (a reference to a deleted file has none: `400`; revise or forget the memory). A given hash confirms that content only: where the file was since seen with another hash, or reported deleted, the reference takes the given one and stays stale (with the hash seen, if any) until the file is reported with that content; for a reference that is not stale, a given hash other than the stored one is a `409` (the file was last known with the stored content: report the file first). Needs `memory:write` and sight of the memory. Audited as `memory.revalidate`.

post.description: File-touched recall (TPL-05), what a coding harness's hook calls. Each file comes with its current content hash (the git blob hash by convention). First the staleness of the memories linked to the files is updated (TPL-04): a reference whose stored hash differs becomes stale, one whose file has its stored content again stops being stale, a rename moves it. Then every linked memory the caller may recall is returned, under the same access decision as `recall`: `memories` (not stale) and `needs_revalidation` (stale: left out of default recall until revalidated, revised or forgotten). With `query`, procedures that match the task are added in `related`. Needs `memory:read`; the staleness is recorded only for a caller that also has `memory:write` (for others the comparison is made for the answer alone). Several states of one file are applied in order. Changes are audited as `memory.stale`, `memory.fresh` and `memory.code_moved`; another hash seen on a reference that is stale already is no change of state, and is audited as `memory.code_seen`.
